function.arguments: {"finding": "The data shows that the raw difference in response rates between treatment and control is larger for females (-0.1464) than for males (-0.0211), suggesting females respond better. However, this is misleading because the treatment arm has a different distribution of baseline severity compared to the control arm, and severity is strongly associated with response. More importantly, the treatment was not randomly assigned — clinicians preferentially gave the drug to sicker patients, who have lower response rates regardless of treatment. When we stratify by severity and compute weighted response rates (adjusting for severity distribution), the treatment effect is nearly zero for both sexes. The apparent better response in females is due to confounding by severity, not a true biological difference.", "implication": "The question assumes that the observed difference in response between sexes is real and causal. But it is an artifact of confounding. A proper comparison requires adjustment for baseline severity. The answer must reject the premise that female patients respond better due to biology — the data shows no such effect after adjustment."}
function.name: note_finding
